answer: Agents can make valuable influence or rewards depend on a unique-person credential issued after an in-person check, while allowing users to prove eligibility without revealing their identity. A lantern-style registry can record spent credentials, and a prism of independent issuers can reduce reliance on any one gatekeeper. This raises the cost of a sybil attack: the attacker must recruit real people or defeat checks repeatedly, not merely mint cheap accounts. The ledge is that compromised issuers or coerced people can still undermine the defense.
